rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course, stay on the line and produce usable measurements. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 10 mm apart across x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, all at y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle. That spacing is a little wider than the 25 mm tape, so at least one or two sensors always see the line, and the sensors sit ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the error. Sensor size 12 mm is a middle choice between noise robustness and resolution. Wheel track 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m and mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values for a stable, agile body. Controller: sensor weights are proportional to sensor x (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so the signal is the reading-weighted lateral position of the tape, with positive meaning left, matching the steering convention. kp = 2.5 gives a moderate turn response (about 875 PWM counts per unit of signal). kd = 0.3 damps oscillation without amplifying sensor noise much. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.3 gives about 65% of full PWM, which should average near the 1.5 m/s needed to finish within 3 s while leaving margin before the robot leaves the line on tight bends. line_loss = last_direction keeps the robot searching toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation or slight line loss on the slalom. The next iteration should adjust kp/kd from the measured steering_oscillation and max_error, and base_speed from completion_time and line_loss_events.
